text:
Alex: Taking handoff in ~20m — quick FYI. I’m seeing a rising alert rate for inference-p95-errors in eu-west-1 over the last 10m. Currently ~6 alerts/min (policy p95>0.5). I’ll be primary for the shift but Morgan was on overnight. Thinking about a short threshold suppression while I triage — any objections?

incident-bot: ALERT: inference-p95-errors (prod-eu) triggered · count=6/min · link=https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/INF-P95-1934567

Jamie: Can you drop the runbook link and confirm who is secondary tonight?

Alex: runbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/inference/alert-tuning#canary-noise. Morgan is secondary until 23:00 UTC. I’m primary until 04:00 UTC. If we change thresholds we should record it in shift notes and incident tracker. I’m leaning to a 30m suppress while I dig in.

Morgan: I’m available for ~30m then offline. If this is an actual SLO breach we shouldn’t suppress. Are we seeing real 5xx or customer errors?

Alex: 5xx metrics are flat. Looks like noise correlated with a recent canary push to the dedupe service. I want to create a short suppression (30m) with a clear reason, monitor, then roll back the canary if needed.

Lee: Prefer rollback over tuning alerts whenever possible. How long does rollback take?

Alex: Rollback + cache flush ~8–10m. I’ll do rollback if alerts exceed 10/min or if any customer traces show increased error rates.

Priya: Quick reminder: manual threshold changes must be announced in #eng-oncall and logged in /incidents. Runbook section 'alert-tuning' recommends short suppressions only for known noisy deploys and to attach justification.

Alex: Totally — will create suppression with reason 'canary noise' and set a 30m TTL. I’ll add notes to the incident tracker and update the runbook pointer.

incident-bot: SUPPRESSION CREATED by Alex · alert=inference-p95-errors · duration=30m · reason="canary noise (deploy id: canary-2026-03-14)" · id=sup-1934567001

Jamie: Assigning secondary to @Morgan for visibility. If suppression doesn’t reduce noise, escalate to SRE rotation and consider rollback. :eyes:

Morgan: Watching logs now — quick tail output:
```
kubectl -n inference logs deploy/dedupe-canary | grep -i timeout | tail -n 5
# repeated timeout at ~200ms, stacktrace entries pointing to dedupe cache
```
Looks related to canary.

Alex: That matches. Starting rollback now. Tag me if paging spikes >12/min. I’ll also update the runbook pointer we referenced.

incident-bot: ROLLBACK JOB STARTED by Alex · target=canary-2026-03-14 · ETA=8m · job_id=rb-1934567012

Lee: If rollback completes and noise drops, let suppression expire naturally but add a note to product about avoiding canary traffic during peak.

incident-bot: ROLLBACK COMPLETE · job_id=rb-1934567012 · status=success · completed_at=1934567390

Alex: Rollback finished. Noise dropped to ~1 alert/min. I’ll close suppression early in 5m unless anything elses pops up. Adding entry to shift notes and the incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-1934567 — mitigation: rollback canary, no customer impact.

Priya: Thanks — please attach the SLO dashboard snapshot and mark as 'no-customer-impact' if confirmed. Also add the suppression justification to the tracker.

Alex: Added dashboard snapshot and wrote: "no impact — mitigation: rollback canary; suppression created to avoid noisy alerts during rollback". Closing the loop now.

Morgan: Thanks — I’ll keep an eye until 23:00 and ping if anything looks off.

Jamie: Nice work. Reminder to update the runbook with a short blurb about canary throttling during peak windows.

Alex: Will do.
